interests.title: Reliable AI systems
interests.description: Making model-backed services resilient, observable, and understandable under real production constraints.

interests.title: Evaluation and benchmarks
interests.description: Using lightweight, repeatable tests to detect quality regressions in retrieval and AI-assisted workflows.

interests.title: Distributed systems for ML
interests.description: Studying latency, consistency, throughput, and infrastructure trade-offs at the AI/backend boundary.

interests.title: Human-AI developer workflows
interests.description: Exploring how AI-assisted development can preserve technical rigor, accountability, and reviewability.

active.title: Evaluation foundations for AI features
active.problem: Ad hoc demonstrations can miss correctness, relevance, and failure-mode regressions that affect real workflows.
active.methodology: Incremental benchmark design: start with representative cases, define failure modes, compare variants, and retain the evidence for later runs.

planned.title: Reliability patterns for agentic systems
planned.problem: Retries, tool failures, partial execution, and timeout behavior need explicit workflow states rather than single-request assumptions.
planned.methodology: Planned experiments will use controlled service and tool failures, explicit workflow states, and trace-based analysis.

planned.title: Decision-aware AI infrastructure
planned.problem: Infrastructure decisions often treat every request as equally certain, even when model confidence or latency budgets vary.
planned.methodology: System experiments would compare routing policies against latency budgets, fallback behavior, and defined success criteria.
